agta/set-1/wind-heart-rescuer-taguwasi.reason: Saklolo ng Hangin gives the wind-and-rescue identity a short, memorable title. It avoids naming a specific wind such as Habagat without supporting lore.

agta/set-1/fifth-sky-tyrant-kalimangalnu.reason: Lupit ng Kalangitan leads with the character's threatening presence. The second option keeps the fifth-heaven setting explicit; the third is a metaphor, not a new creature trait.

agta/set-1/life-breath-mother-nanolay.reason: Hininga ng Buhay is a compact identity rather than a literal description of a mother. The alternatives emphasize care and life without assigning new powers.

babaylan/set-1/mountain-sovereign-maria-.reason: Diwa ng Kabundukan evokes the mountain presence already established by the card. The alternatives suggest sovereignty without adding a new family relationship or historical claim.

babaylan/set-1/harvest-warden-mangaw.reason: Biyaya ng Ani gives the harvest guardian a warm, distinctive identity. The alternatives shift the emphasis to protection or abundance.

babaylan/set-1/thunder-sovereign-kaptan.reason: Dagundong ng Langit communicates authority through thunder itself, without using another long Pinuno or Tagapag title.

babaylan/set-1/ocean-sovereign-maguayan.reason: Tinig ng Laot gives the ocean ruler a quieter but commanding identity. The other options emphasize the sea's presence or dominion.

babaylan/set-1/abyssal-revolt-sinogo.reason: Himagsik ng Kalaliman reads as an identity rather than a translated sentence. It preserves the card's rebellion-and-depths theme without inventing its cause.

babaylan/set-1/last-moon-devourer-bakuna.reason: Gutom sa Buwan makes the moon-devouring motif immediate. It does not claim that every tradition shares the card's last-moon storyline.

babaylan/set-1/unbroken-invocation-amara.reason: Panatang Di-Matitinag gives the unbroken invocation an emotional identity. The alternatives keep the emphasis on the voice and persistence of the calling.

maguindanao/set-1/nonok-veiled-guardian-.reason: Kalinga ng Nonok preserves the distinctive Nonok association and guardian role. The alternatives are imagery, not claims about a new ritual.

maguindanao/set-1/beneath-water-ancestre.reason: Alaala sa Kailaliman ties ancestry to the underwater setting in a short title. It avoids inventing an additional royal rank or origin story.

maguindanao/set-1/boat-watching-tonong-t.reason: Kalinga sa Paglalayag emphasizes what the boat guardian means to travelers, rather than literally describing someone watching boats. The third option retains Tonong explicitly.

maguindanao/set-1/sun-darkening-scourge-.reason: Lilim ng Araw is brief and ominous, grounded in the repository's story of Pah's wings darkening the sky. The alternatives emphasize the wings or the sky.

maguindanao/set-1/rattan-haunt-scourge-k.reason: Sindak sa Yantok anchors the threat in the card's rattan setting. Kabalalan is the associated setting in the existing set, while the last option emphasizes atmosphere.

maguindanao/set-1/matutun-branch-devoure.reason: Poot ng Matutun draws on the repository's account of the monster fighting with torn branches on Matutun. It avoids amplifying the old title into an unsupported branch-eating claim.

maguindanao/set-1/land-restoring-raja-in.reason: Panata ng Pagbangon centers the restoration of people and land in the repository's story. The second choice retains Raja as an explicit cultural title.

maguindanao/set-1/gurayen-wrath-mate-mak.reason: Katuwang ng Poot emphasizes the wrath-mate identity without asserting a specific marriage or family relationship not established in the available notes.

maguindanao/set-1/three-scourge-champion.reason: Tapang na May Kapalit reflects the repository's story: Sulayman defeats the creatures, but Pah's falling wing crushes him. The alternatives emphasize courage or the three victories.

maguindanao/set-1/seven-sight-final-scou.reason: Pitong Tanaw ng Sindak evokes the seven-sight threat without claiming new anatomy. Huling Anino is the shortest option and retains the final-scourge mood.
